clue.text: Liking one sort of swan song

parts.note: a pen is a female swan
a chant is a song, as in plainchant

explanation.surface: A fondness for one particular kind of farewell performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swan song' looks like one phrase meaning a final performance, but the two words must be split and read separately.
explanation.definitionFit: A penchant is a strong inclination or fondness, a synonym of liking.

clue.text: Sounds like I clean up rubbish

indicators.note: Sounds like says the phrase given is pronounced the same as the entry

parts.note: I wash means I clean up

explanation.surface: A person announces they will tidy away the trash.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyewash is slang for nonsense or humbug, a synonym of rubbish as talk.

clue.text: Lake on Swiss border with Italian viewpoint

parts.note: con is Italian for with
a stance is an attitude or point of view

explanation.surface: A lake straddling Switzerland's frontier, seen from an Italian perspective.
explanation.definitionFit: Lake Constance lies where Switzerland, Germany and Austria meet.

clue.text: On board a delivery vehicle

parts.note: a float is a small vehicle, as in a milk float, a British electric milk delivery van

explanation.surface: Riding on a delivery van.
explanation.walkthrough: A milk float is a slow British electric van that delivers milk to doorsteps.
explanation.definitionFit: Afloat means at sea or on a ship, which is what on board means.

clue.text: Force needed to open 6 ac, 12 and 25

definitions.text: Force needed to open 6 ac, 12 and 25

parts.words: Force needed to open 6 ac, 12 and 25
parts.note: the abbreviation of this force is the two letters that start 6 across, 12 across and 25 across

explanation.surface: Troops are required to break into three places.
explanation.walkthrough: The Territorial Army is Britain's volunteer reserve; its initials TA open TACTIC, TATTOO and TAURUS.
explanation.definitionFit: The Territorial Army was the British Army's volunteer reserve force.

clue.text: Diplomacy I see as sound manoeuvre

parts.note: tact is diplomacy, delicacy in dealing with people

indicators.note: as sound tells us to write the word see by how it is pronounced, as a single letter

parts.note: the word see is pronounced like the letter C

explanation.surface: A diplomat regards tact as a sensible move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like an adjective meaning sensible; it tells you to use the letter that is pronounced like 'see'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tactic is a planned move or ploy, the same as a manoeuvre.

clue.text: Gossip as source of inspiration for Rossini?

explanation.surface: Rumour as the spark for a composer's work.
explanation.walkthrough: Rossini wrote the opera William Tell, so a tale about Tell inspired him.
explanation.definitionFit: A telltale is a person who reports others' secrets, a gossip; and the Tell legend is the story behind Rossini's opera.

clue.text: Order the list amended

indicators.note: amended means the letters of the list are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: An instruction to correct a list.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' looks like a command; it is the Order of the Thistle, Scotland's order of chivalry.
explanation.definitionFit: The Most Ancient and Most Noble Order of the Thistle is a Scottish chivalric order.

clue.text: Pact agreed at battlefield in Massachusetts first

indicators.note: first means the battlefield's name comes before the word at

parts.note: Concord, Massachusetts was the site of an opening battle of the American Revolution

explanation.surface: A treaty signed on a historic American battlefield.
explanation.definitionFit: A concordat is a formal agreement, especially between the Vatican and a state.

clue.text: Simple sense about names

indicators.note: about means the word for sense goes around the abbreviation

parts.note: to feel is to sense
N is the abbreviation for name, so NN stands for names

explanation.surface: Plain common sense about what things are called.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Simple' looks like an adjective; it is the old noun for a medicinal herb, which fennel is.
explanation.definitionFit: A simple is an old word for a medicinal plant or herb, and fennel is such a herb.

clue.text: Persuasion to give £1, in part

indicators.note: in means the money letters are placed inside the word for part

parts.note: a region is a part or area
£ is L (from Latin libra, a pound) and 1 is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Trying to talk someone into paying a pound towards something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Persuasion' looks like the act of coaxing; it means a religious faith, as in 'of the Catholic persuasion'.
explanation.definitionFit: A persuasion is a set of beliefs, especially a faith or denomination.

clue.text: With old man's transport I collected beef

parts.note: the old man is father, pa, so old man's gives pa's
a tram is a form of transport

explanation.surface: Someone collects cured meat using their dad's vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastrami is highly seasoned smoked beef.

clue.text: Belligerent finish at excessively military display

indicators.note: finish points to the closing letter of the word Belligerent

parts.note: too means excessively, as in too much

explanation.surface: An aggressive end to an over-militaristic parade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Belligerent finish' reads as a fierce ending; it is just the last letter of 'Belligerent'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tattoo is an evening military display of marching and music, such as the Edinburgh Tattoo.

clue.text: Ring keeps Penny and husband, united

parts.note: united as one: one means joined together

explanation.surface: A wedding ring holds a couple, Penny and her husband, together.
explanation.definitionFit: To ring someone is to call them on the telephone, so the verb ring is a synonym.

clue.text: Feasible examination

explanation.surface: A test that can actually be done.
explanation.definitionFit: Practical means workable or realistic; a practical is also a hands-on exam, as in a science lab test.

clue.text: Bitter about Alfred getting situation of mine

indicators.note: about means the word for bitter goes around the name

parts.note: bitter weather is cold
Alfie is a familiar form of the name Alfred

explanation.surface: A resentful Alfred lands a job down the pit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bitter' looks like a mood or an ale; it is the weather sense, cold.
explanation.definitionFit: A coalfield is the region where coal mines are located, the setting of a mine.

clue.text: Pat's 25 — what a silly thing to say!

definitions.text: what a silly thing to say!

parts.note: Pat is the stock name for an Irishman, so Pat's means Irish
25 across is the zodiac sign whose symbol is the bull

explanation.surface: An Irishman's star sign reacts to a foolish remark.
explanation.walkthrough: An Irish bull is a self-contradictory statement, as in 'If you don't get this letter, write and tell me'.
explanation.definitionFit: An Irish bull is a ludicrous, self-contradictory remark.

clue.text: Secretive in the last resort, at end of day

indicators.note: resort is read as re-sort, so the letters of the last are sorted again
end of points to the closing letter of the word day

explanation.surface: Being cagey, as a last resort, when the day is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' is read as re-sort: THE LAST becomes STEALTH, then Y from the end of 'day'.
explanation.definitionFit: Stealthy means furtive and covert, acting so as not to be noticed.

clue.text: Discover Cartesian error

indicators.note: error means the letters of Cartesian are in the wrong order and need rearranging

explanation.surface: Someone spots a mistake in Descartes's reasoning.
explanation.definitionFit: To ascertain is to find out for certain, so it means discover.

clue.text: Shows inclination in church to have a purge

indicators.note: in means the inclination word goes inside the abbreviation for church

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
leans means tilts or shows an inclination

explanation.surface: A congregation leans towards a clear-out.
explanation.definitionFit: To cleanse is to purify or rid of impurities, which is what purge means as a verb.

clue.text: Highest-ranking duke embraces king

indicators.note: embraces means the word for duke wraps around the letter for king

parts.note: dukes is slang for fists, so a duke is a fist
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: The most senior duke hugs the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duke' is a nobleman on the surface; in slang 'put up your dukes' means raise your fists.
explanation.definitionFit: First means top-ranked, ahead of all others.

clue.text: Browning rashly produces this paper flower

parts.note: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper
a flower is something that flows, a river; a burn is a Scottish stream

explanation.surface: A poet's hasty work yields a newspaper bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Browning' suggests the poet, and 'flower' a bloom; really it is tanning rashly, and a flower is a thing that flows.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting brown in the sun too rashly leaves a painful reddened skin.

clue.text: City gent, socially acceptable in 5

parts.note: a gent is a man

indicators.note: in means the letter for socially acceptable goes inside the abbreviation of 5's answer

parts.note: 5 down is the Territorial Army, abbreviated TA, Britain's volunteer reserve
U means upper-class or socially acceptable, from Nancy Mitford's U and non-U

explanation.surface: A City of London businessman who is respectable and serves in the reserves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'City gent' looks like one phrase for a London financier; split it: City is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Mantua is a city in Lombardy, northern Italy.

clue.text: Girl's position of leadership in 5

indicators.note: in means the leadership word sits inside the abbreviation of 5's answer

parts.note: 5 down is the Territorial Army, abbreviated TA, a British volunteer reserve force
the helm is the position of control or leadership

explanation.surface: A young woman holds a command post in the reserve army.
explanation.walkthrough: The TA (Territorial Army) is Britain's part-time volunteer army reserve; 'Girl's' is 'Girl is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Thelma is a female first name, so an example of a girl.

clue.text: Behold an object producing disgust

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or behold
an gives A, the indefinite article
a thing is an object

explanation.surface: Look at something that makes you feel sick.
explanation.definitionFit: Loathing is intense dislike or revulsion, much the same as disgust.

clue.text: Turn wine about in container

parts.note: C stands for circa, Latin for about

indicators.note: Turn means the wine's name is read from back to front

parts.note: retsina is a Greek resinated wine

explanation.surface: Swirl wine around in a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn' reads the Greek wine backwards to give ANISTER; 'about' looks like the reversal signal too, but it supplies C for circa.
explanation.definitionFit: A canister is a small cylindrical box or tin, a type of container.

clue.text: Sign he's got out of reference book

indicators.note: got out of means the letters of he's are removed from the book's name

parts.note: a thesaurus is a reference book of synonyms

explanation.surface: A man has found a signpost by looking it up in a book.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking HES out of THESAURUS leaves T-AURUS; 'got out of' looks like fetched from, but it means removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Taurus is one of the twelve signs of the zodiac.

clue.text: General means to make room for manoeuvre

parts.note: Robert E. Lee was the Confederate general in the American Civil War
a way is a means of doing something

explanation.surface: A commander's method for clearing space for troops to move.
explanation.definitionFit: Leeway is freedom of action or margin, the latitude to move.

clue.text: A grey in first part of life, perhaps

definitions.text: A grey in first part of life, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters given may be arranged differently
first part of points to the opening letter of the word life

explanation.surface: A grey horse in its early youth.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of 'A grey in' plus L (first part of 'life') are rearranged; the whole clue also describes the answer, a young horse that might be grey.
explanation.definitionFit: A yearling is an animal, especially a horse, in its first year, and a grey is a horse colour.
